CausalChain: Dual-localized lncRNA expression -> In the nucleus, lncRNAs bind transcription factors/chromatin remodelers -> altered expression of immune modulatory cytokines and checkpoint molecules -> creation of an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment -> In the cytoplasm, the same lncRNAs act as miRNA sponges -> dysregulation of translation of proteins involved in antigen processing/immune activation -> further immune evasion; Combined ASO/siRNA targeting -> restoration of proper lncRNA levels and distribution -> reactivation of immune surveillance and increased sensitivity to immunotherapy
Hypothesis: Dual-localized lncRNAs drive tumor immune escape by concurrently reprogramming nuclear transcriptional profiles and sequestering regulatory miRNAs in the cytoplasm; thus, precise dual targeting of these lncRNAs will restore antitumor immunity and improve outcomes in immunotherapy-resistant cancers.
Abstract: Recent advances in lncRNA research have uncovered diverse roles for these transcripts in both nuclear gene regulation and cytoplasmic post‐transcriptional control, suggesting that lncRNAs with dual localization serve as integrative hubs in tumor biology. We propose that such dual-localized lncRNAs not only modulate oncogenic signaling pathways but also orchestrate immune escape mechanisms via coordinated regulation of immune checkpoint gene expression and miRNA sponging. By simultaneously targeting their nuclear and cytoplasmic functions using combined ASO/siRNA strategies, it may be possible to reprogram tumor immunogenicity and enhance the efficacy of existing immunotherapies. This integrated approach opens avenues for precision gene therapy in resistant cancers.
